title: List of prime ministers of Canada
summary:
This document is a portion of a Wikipedia article titled "List of prime ministers of Canada" that covers several key aspects of the Canadian prime ministership. It begins by defining the role of the prime minister as the head of government of Canada, noting that twenty-four people have served in this position, and explains the appointment process—where the prime minister is formally appointed by the governor general but, by constitutional convention, must hold the confidence of the elected House of Commons. It identifies Mark Carney as the current (24th) prime minister, having taken office on 14 March 2025, and mentions six living former prime ministers.

The document then includes a "Model" section explaining that the office is not defined in Canada's written constitution but exists through constitutional convention, modeled after the British system; it notes John A. Macdonald formed the first government on 1 July 1867. A "Term" section describes how prime ministerial terms are determined, including the history of oath-taking (mandatory since 1957), changes in resignation procedures since 1920, and the Interpretation Act of 1967. It also notes that only two prime ministers—John A. Macdonald and John Thompson—died in office.

Additionally, the document explains the Canadian convention of counting prime ministers by individuals rather than terms (24 individuals forming 30 ministries), references a lifespan timeline, and concludes with a list of related articles ("See also" section) and external links to resources about Canadian prime ministers.
